newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up on higher inflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up on higher inflows.

text.p: * Central Bank biggest buyer of dollars
The Philippine peso continued to gather strength on Tuesday, boosted by inflows in the form of remittances from overseas contract workers and portfolio investments, traders said.
The peso closed at 26.253 to the dollar versus 26.262.
"Portfolio money is coming in for positioning ahead of the expected credit upgrading of the Philippines next year," a dealer from a local bank said.
Inflows in the form of remittances from overseas workers have started to pour in time for Christmas spending.
The day's average was at 26.255 from 26.260. Market volume rose to $202.90 million from $185.20 million.
Traders said the Central Bank intervened in the market by purchasing dollars to limit the peso's strength which reached a day-high of 26.247.
The Central Bank bought some $53 million at 26.25 to 26.252, a trader from a large bank estimated. It also purchased $92 million on Monday at 26.257 to 26.26.
